concerns.title: Canonical SDL source profile
concerns.definition: Source uses the governed SDL YAML profile and safe loading rules.

concerns.title: Closed structural model
concerns.definition: Authored fields conform to the published closed SDL document model.

concerns.title: Semantic reference integrity
concerns.definition: Named references and cross-section constraints pass semantic validation.

concerns.title: Topology and resource intent
concerns.definition: Scenario topology, resources, services, identities, and relationships are authored as intent.

concerns.title: Authored and observed state separation
concerns.definition: Authored intent, realized state, observation, and evidence remain distinct claim planes.

concerns.title: Scoped specificity and open-world intent
concerns.definition: Exact, constrained, and open realization posture is explicit at the governed scope.

concerns.title: Parameter typing
concerns.definition: Scenario parameters have typed finite or constrained domains and portable bindings.

concerns.title: Experimental factor declaration
concerns.definition: Controlled factors and levels are declared separately from scenario substitution.

concerns.title: Controlled allocation
concerns.definition: Conditions, blocking factors, assignment units, and replication allocation are declared.

concerns.title: Randomization policy
concerns.definition: Random assignment or sampling policy and its scope are declared.

concerns.title: Seed preservation
concerns.definition: Relevant seed, generator, scheduler, and sampling controls are preserved with provenance.

concerns.title: Backend-neutral propositions
concerns.definition: Claims over stable subjects use typed backend-neutral predicates and evidence bases.

concerns.title: Role-constrained assertions
concerns.definition: Preconditions, invariants, and postconditions reference propositions with explicit polarity.

concerns.title: Condition-to-proposition binding
concerns.definition: Executable probes are bindings and do not redefine proposition truth.
concerns.semantic_owner: SDL conditions and runtime truth results

concerns.title: Workflow compensation
concerns.definition: Authored workflows can name bounded compensation behavior for failed steps.

concerns.title: Backend teardown and reconciliation
concerns.definition: Realizers disclose and execute bounded resource cleanup and reconciliation.

concerns.title: Manual and advanced rollback
concerns.definition: Operators can author or invoke rollback beyond bounded workflow compensation.

concerns.title: Time-domain declaration
concerns.definition: Wall, monotonic, logical, simulation, and scenario time domains are explicit.

concerns.title: Clock declaration
concerns.definition: Clock identity, origin, rate, and ownership are declared.

concerns.title: Temporal ordering and causality
concerns.definition: Ordering, causality, concurrency, and partial-order claims have governed semantics.

concerns.title: Deadlines and windows
concerns.definition: Deadlines, evaluation windows, and temporal bounds use declared time domains.

concerns.title: Pacing and synchronization
concerns.definition: Advancement, pacing, synchronization, and drift policy are explicit.

concerns.title: Participant declaration
concerns.definition: Participant identity, role, operating scope, and authority anchors are explicit.

concerns.title: Participant action and observation surfaces
concerns.definition: Visible actions, perceptions, observation boundaries, and histories are governed.

concerns.title: Participant episode and reset
concerns.definition: Episode identity, initialization, reset, termination, and provenance are portable.

concerns.title: Participant budgets
concerns.definition: Action, time, cost, token, and other quotas have exhaustion semantics and accounting.

concerns.title: Reference trajectories
concerns.definition: Demonstrations and trajectories have typed references, lineage, splits, and replay limits.

concerns.title: Hidden benchmark assets
concerns.definition: Gold standards and hidden assets have controlled visibility and provenance.

concerns.title: Verifier and adjudication
concerns.definition: Verifier, judge, annotation, disagreement, and adjudication assets are governed.

concerns.title: Graded reward in SDL
concerns.definition: Graded reward and scoring are not authored as scenario truth semantics.

concerns.title: Evaluation outcome evidence
concerns.definition: Outcome interpretation, measures, evidence, and evaluation results retain provenance.

concerns.title: Credential intent
concerns.definition: Intentional scenario identities and credential posture are distinct from operator secrets.

concerns.title: Credential materialization
concerns.definition: Credential-bearing setup is materialized and evidenced without exposing operator secrets.

concerns.title: Host architecture constraints
concerns.definition: CPU architecture and host-level compatibility requirements are portable constraints.

concerns.title: Substrate constraints
concerns.definition: Backend, hypervisor, container, network, and apparatus constraints are explicit.

concerns.title: Vulnerability inventory
concerns.definition: Declared vulnerabilities and weaknesses use governed identifiers and affected subjects.

concerns.title: Weakness and exploitability semantics
concerns.definition: Classification, reachability, exploitability, and observation claims remain distinct.

concerns.title: Flexible step tooling
concerns.definition: Workflow steps can bind tools without making backend-native names portable behavior.

concerns.title: Portable behavior contracts
concerns.definition: Behavior is expressed through preconditions, effects, failures, interactions, and governed action contracts.

concerns.title: Behavioral relation taxonomy
concerns.definition: Conformance, refinement, trace, observational, bisimulation, epistemic, and strategic relations are not conflated.

concerns.title: Apparatus constraints and context
concerns.definition: Scientific claims bind to declared apparatus requirements and realized context.

concerns.title: Run plan
concerns.definition: Pre-run episode, stochastic, allocation, and stopping intent is versioned.

concerns.title: Study and benchmark record
concerns.definition: Study questions, membership, allocation, analysis plan, and validity notes are archived.

concerns.title: Evidence provenance
concerns.definition: Captured evidence, measures, artifacts, and derivations remain attributable and integrity-bound.

profiles.title: Valid SDL fragment
profiles.intended_claim: The document is admitted as a structurally and semantically valid SDL authoring fragment.
explicit_non_claims: Does not claim deployability, realization, experimental control, reproducibility, backend conformance, or behavioral equivalence.

behavioral_claims.subject: An artifact admitted by the valid-sdl-fragment profile
behavioral_claims.evidence_boundary: Parser and semantic validator acceptance for the submitted SDL artifact under its declared profile.
limitations: Acceptance applies only to the submitted artifact and the declared SDL profile revision.
explicit_non_claims: Semantic validity does not establish backend realization or behavioral equivalence.

profiles.title: Deployable scenario intent
profiles.intended_claim: The authored scenario carries sufficient portable intent to request realization subject to an explicit apparatus and backend envelope.
explicit_non_claims: Does not claim that every backend can realize the scenario, that deployment succeeded, or that realized behavior is equivalent.

behavioral_claims.subject: An artifact assessed against deployable-scenario-intent
behavioral_claims.evidence_boundary: The required concern dispositions for one candidate artifact and its named external contract witnesses.
limitations: Profile satisfaction is conditional on every required concern and external witness; it says nothing about execution.
explicit_non_claims: No backend realization, trace inclusion, or equivalence claim.

profiles.title: Participant-evaluation scenario
profiles.intended_claim: The scenario and bound experiment contracts define participant-visible work, perception, action, episode control, and outcome evidence for evaluation.
explicit_non_claims: Does not claim participant implementations are strategically equivalent, that hidden global state is visible, or that finite probes prove bisimulation.

behavioral_claims.subject: An artifact assessed against participant-evaluation-scenario
behavioral_claims.evidence_boundary: The required concern dispositions and contract witnesses for one bound participant-evaluation scenario.
limitations: Profile satisfaction records declared evaluation structure; observed participant histories require a separate projection-bound comparison.
explicit_non_claims: No projected-history, epistemic, strategic, or bisimulation equivalence claim.

profiles.title: Controlled experiment scenario
profiles.intended_claim: The scenario is bound to a pre-run design with controlled variation, allocation, apparatus, timing, capture, and analysis intent.
explicit_non_claims: Does not claim causal validity, successful execution, adequate power, reproducibility, or backend behavioral equivalence.

behavioral_claims.subject: An artifact assessed against controlled-experiment-scenario
behavioral_claims.evidence_boundary: The pre-run design declarations and required concern witnesses for one controlled-experiment input.
limitations: Design completeness precedes execution and cannot establish empirical adequacy or causal validity.
explicit_non_claims: No empirical adequacy, statistical equivalence, trace equivalence, or bisimulation claim.

profiles.title: Reproducible benchmark or study input
profiles.intended_claim: The scenario and governed experiment bundle preserve sufficient design, apparatus, participant, evidence, lineage, and analysis context for a bounded reproduction attempt.
explicit_non_claims: Does not guarantee bitwise replay, equal outcomes, scientific validity, generalizability, or behavioral equivalence across apparatuses.

behavioral_claims.subject: An artifact assessed against reproducible-benchmark-study-input
behavioral_claims.evidence_boundary: The preserved design, apparatus, participant, evidence, lineage, and analysis declarations for one benchmark or study input.
limitations: Input completeness supports a bounded reproduction attempt but does not establish the outcome of that attempt.
explicit_non_claims: No empirical adequacy, statistical equivalence, behavioral equivalence, or generalizability claim.
